title: Standalone restricted and public sharing without a hosted control plane (Fixture F1)

programme.revalidation_owner: victornife (maintainer; re-run affected rows on protocol/auth/trust/lifecycle release changes and on first published release package containing #641/#642/#581)

baseline.release_package_note: Locally built development distribution from pinned merged main (52b09adfbccfc3b14a86ce48a2de06395a7fae70). Not a published or Sigstore-attested release archive; released-product claims require revalidation on the eventual published release containing #641, #642, and #581.

historical_published_baseline.reason: Published v2.2.0 predates #641 (declared intent, §9.5 audience-delta classes, §9.4 postconditions) and #642 (#563/#562 complete withdrawal and exact-entry retirement).

build.command: CGO_ENABLED=0 GOOS=linux GOARCH=arm64 go build -trimpath -ldflags "-s -w -X main.version=v2.2.0-dev+52b09adfbccf" -tags "brotli zstd acme console otel grpc http3 importer wasmplugins stream consul kubernetes waf" -o jul ./cmd/jul

authentication.description: HTTP Basic (bcrypt htpasswd) + WAF on dashboard; anonymous + rate-limit on portal; shared listener 192.0.2.10:443

TLS client_auth.mode = 'request' on shared 192.0.2.10:443 + require_client_cert = true and Basic on dashboard (composed); emits client_auth_request_mode_shared warning because browsers with client certs may prompt on portal
Portal on 192.0.2.10:443 (client_auth off) and dashboard on separate listener 192.0.2.10:8443 with default-deny-mtls + client_auth.mode = 'require' + require_client_cert = true

protocol.notes: Jul -> plaintext origin uses HTTP/1.1 by contract (spec §12).

not_applicable_combinations.reason: Contractual protocol boundary (ADR 0018 §17, spec §12): Jul implements RFC 6455 HTTP/1.1 Upgrade only and does not implement RFC 8441 / RFC 9220 Extended CONNECT.

protocol.reason: Spec §12 and §18 explicitly classify native gRPC, HTTP/3, and L4 [[stream]] as outside mandatory F1 fixture traffic; covered by existing owner suites (TestLongLivedNativeGRPCReloadAndShutdown, internal/server/grpc_retirement_test.go, internal/server/http3_mtls_test.go).

resource_qualification_policy.rationale_for_reuse_across_authority_and: Full W0–W4 resource and continuity qualification (15m W0 idle, 12m W1 representative 70/10/20 mix, W2 mixed + 10% excluded + 20 held long-lived dashboard streams, W3 2m complete withdrawal + 1 req/s portal continuity probe, W4 60s backend outage + recovery + >=90s drain + 2m post-drain comparison) is executed on CFG-F1-04/CFG-F1-05 under the hardened systemd service profile on the pinned full-profile binary. (1) Authority equivalence: file-owned configurations (CFG-F1-10, CFG-F1-11, CFG-F1-12, CFG-F1-13) differ only in the control-plane desired-state writer (SIGHUP/file-watcher vs /api/v1/config/apply) and compile the exact same runtime handler tree. (2) Authentication & listener cost dominance: CFG-F1-04 executes per-request HTTP Basic bcrypt verification plus Coraza OWASP CRS WAF inspection on every dashboard request, which strictly dominates per-request CPU and heap allocation compared to mTLS (CFG-F1-08/CFG-F1-12 shared listener and CFG-F1-09/CFG-F1-13 dedicated :8443 listener, where X.509 chain verification runs once per TLS handshake and per-request enforcement is an in-memory atomic pointer + serial-map CRL lookup in clientAuthBundle; a second listener on :8443 adds 1 accept goroutine and 1 socket FD). Resource reuse never substitutes for functional, security, isolation, retirement, or recovery verification: all authority and mTLS variants execute their own real-client functional, security, held-stream retirement, recovery, and cgroup/RSS/FD snapshot checks.

cases.description: Service profile hardening & collision-refusing setup: systemd jul.service running as unprivileged jul:jul user with ProtectSystem=strict, NoNewPrivileges=yes, PrivateTmp=yes, PrivateDevices=yes, MemoryDenyWriteExecute=yes, and 0700/0600 directory/file modes; lean binary rejects WAF before persistence.
cases.expected_outcome: systemctl show verifies user/group/hardening properties; lean jul check exits 1 rejecting WAF; full jul starts cleanly.

cases.description: Safe Step 1 — Loopback preview isolation: default-deny, portal, and dashboard bound to 127.0.0.1:443; host loopback reaches portal and dashboard; external routed namespaces lab-client-1 (192.0.2.11) and lab-client-2 (192.0.2.12) cannot connect to 192.0.2.10:443.
cases.expected_outcome: Host loopback GET portal and dashboard return 200; lab-client-1 and lab-client-2 TCP/TLS connects to 192.0.2.10:443 fail (connection refused).

cases.description: Safe Step 2 — Add Basic check and declare dashboard restricted on loopback: adopt initial baseline, preview and apply CFG-F1-02; verify audience delta class 'narrowed' on dashboard and postcondition 'candidate_serving'; verify intended Basic credentials 200 and missing/wrong credentials 401 on loopback before any LAN bind.
cases.expected_outcome: Plan reports dashboard class=narrowed; apply outcome=applied_live; postcondition result=candidate_serving (candidate=serving, access=matches); loopback unauthenticated/wrong-pass GET dash.lab.test -> 401 (origin_delta=0); intended credentials -> 200.

cases.description: Safe Step 3 — Declare portal public on loopback: preview and apply CFG-F1-03; verify portal-home class 'metadata_only' (declared_mode_widened=true, triggers_retirement=false) and dashboard unchanged.
cases.expected_outcome: Plan reports portal-home class=metadata_only, triggers_retirement=false; apply outcome=applied_live; postcondition result=candidate_serving.

cases.description: Safe Step 4 & 5 — Move all three blocks from 127.0.0.1:443 to 192.0.2.10:443 in one candidate and immediately verify LAN isolation: plan names all three entries as 'uncertain'; zero intermediate unprotected dashboard state on 192.0.2.10:443; lab-client-2 immediately gets 401 on dashboard and 200 on portal; lab-client-1 gets 200 on dashboard with credentials.
cases.expected_outcome: Plan names default-deny, portal-home, and dashboard as class=uncertain; apply outcome=applied_live; postcondition result=candidate_serving; lab-client-2 GET dash.lab.test -> 401 (origin_delta=0), GET portal.lab.test -> 200; lab-client-1 GET dash.lab.test with Basic -> 200.

cases.description: RBAC and S17-1 postcondition disclosure enforcement: auditor (status:read only) refused 403 on GET /api/sharing and POST /api/sharing/postcondition/evaluate; viewer (status:read+config:read) allowed on GET /api/sharing and postcondition evaluate, refused 403 on plan/apply; operator (config:write+config:apply, no config:raw) receives postcondition.status=unavailable (caller_lacks_config_raw) on raw-candidate plan and postcondition.status=available on visible typed patch; admin (config:raw) receives postcondition.status=available on raw-candidate plan.
cases.expected_outcome: All RBAC status codes and postcondition availability states match contract with zero state change during read/refusal probes.

cases.description: Managed CAS, idempotency, stale base, opaque-input reload, and no_change: re-applying opaque-input-free candidate CFG-F1-14 returns outcome=no_change while re-applying file-backed CFG-F1-04 returns outcome=applied_live (re-reading dashboard.htpasswd per hasOpaqueReloadInputs); replaying same Idempotency-Key returns cached terminal result; reusing same Idempotency-Key with different payload returns 409 idempotency_key_reused; stale base_version returns 409 base_version_conflict.
cases.expected_outcome: CFG-F1-14 identical re-apply returns outcome=no_change; CFG-F1-04 re-apply returns outcome=applied_live; idempotency replay returns 200 with same apply_id; mismatched reuse and stale base return 409 before side effects.

cases.description: Managed invalid-candidate rejection and pre-Publish restoration (not_applied): candidate with sharing block on route without route_id is rejected with 422/400 validation error; candidate with unbindable listener address fails preflight/Prepare without mutating serving state.
cases.expected_outcome: Invalid sharing candidate rejected before persistence; serving_version and config_state=managed_clean remain intact.

cases.description: Managed drift detection and explicit resolution: external edit to server.toml transitions config_state to managed_drift; ordinary managed apply is refused with 409 drift_detected while Jul keeps serving; explicit adopt-external preview + confirm (or revert) restores managed_clean without silent force-apply.
cases.expected_outcome: GET /api/v1/status reports config_state=managed_drift; apply refused with 409; adopt-external preview/confirm succeeds and returns to managed_clean.

cases.description: Managed stage_restart, saved-vs-serving layers, and post-restart postcondition lifecycle: stage a restart-required change (e.g. cache.enabled=true or history_dir change); verify config_state=managed_pending_restart, GET /api/sharing exposes both serving and saved layers with distinct revisions, and pre-restart postcondition evaluates to result=not_serving_yet (candidate=base_serving).
cases.expected_outcome: GET /api/sharing shows serving and saved layers; postcondition evaluate returns result=not_serving_yet, candidate=base_serving.

cases.description: Post-restart postcondition key rotation, open long-lived connection shutdown, and recovery: restart Jul while holding an active SSE stream and H1 WebSocket connection; verify clean connection termination on restart, boot_id rotation, and pre-restart postcondition evaluating to result=unverifiable (candidate=unverifiable); re-plan the same raw candidate (with config:raw) and repeatable typed op (location_set_withdrawn) to obtain candidate_serving; verify non-repeatable location_add postcondition reports repeatable=false with manual reconciliation guidance.
cases.expected_outcome: Held SSE/WS connections close cleanly on restart; original postcondition returns result=unverifiable after restart; re-planned raw candidate and repeatable typed op return result=candidate_serving; non-repeatable location_add postcondition reports repeatable=false and manual reconciliation guidance.

cases.description: Postcondition access_matches, diverged, and other_revision separation: (1) apply an unrelated edit (e.g. global.log_level='debug') after CFG-F1-04 -> evaluating CFG-F1-04's postcondition returns result=access_matches (candidate=other_revision, access=matches); (2) apply an access-changing edit (withdrawn=true on dashboard) -> evaluating CFG-F1-04's postcondition returns result=diverged (candidate=other_revision, access=differs, differing_fields=['withdrawn']); (3) evaluate a global-only plan postcondition against another revision -> returns result=other_revision (candidate=other_revision, access=none_expected).
cases.expected_outcome: Exact-candidate and access-fact answers are reported separately across access_matches, diverged, and other_revision; no bare 'confirmed' string.

cases.description: Managed history rollback: preview rollback diff (observing its own audience delta class 'widened' when rolling back from withdrawn CFG-F1-05 to active CFG-F1-04) and execute POST /api/config/rollback.
cases.expected_outcome: Rollback diff shows dashboard class=widened; POST /api/config/rollback succeeds and restores intended dashboard 200 access.

cases.description: File-owned authority boundary, all mutation refusals, SIGHUP reload, and owner rollback: under jul-readonly.service (CFG-F1-10), GET /api/sharing and POST /api/v1/config/plan succeed; POST /api/v1/config/apply, POST /api/config/patch/apply, POST /api/v1/config/rollback, POST /api/config/rollback, POST /api/v1/config/adopt-external, and CLI jul apply are all refused with 409 config_authority_read_only (CLI exit code 6) and zero file modification; owner replaces file with CFG-F1-11 and sends SIGHUP -> withdrawal goes live and postcondition returns candidate_serving; owner reverts to CFG-F1-10 + SIGHUP -> access restored without minting route_id or managed history.
cases.expected_outcome: All remote mutations (apply, patch, rollback, adopt, CLI apply) refused with 409 config_authority_read_only; SIGHUP reload publishes CFG-F1-11 and evaluates candidate_serving; owner revert + SIGHUP restores CFG-F1-10.

cases.description: Reproducible bounded applied_degraded outcome in file_owned mode: bind a local TCP socket on an auxiliary port, reload a file_owned candidate that sets withdrawn=true on dashboard AND adds a [[stream]] listener on that occupied port; HTTP Publish succeeds (dashboard withdrawal is immediately effective, 403 Forbidden) while post-Publish stream reload fails, yielding last_reload.outcome=applied_degraded.
cases.expected_outcome: GET /api/v1/status reports last_reload.outcome='applied_degraded', published=true, http.status='ok', stream.status='failed'; dashboard returns 403 Forbidden with Cache-Control: no-store.

cases.description: Simultaneous anonymous portal success, intended dashboard success, and excluded dashboard denial from independent routed client namespaces.
cases.expected_outcome: lab-client-2 anonymous GET https://portal.lab.test/ -> 200 (portal marker); lab-client-1 Basic GET https://dash.lab.test/api/summary -> 200 (dashboard marker, origin_delta=+1); lab-client-2 anonymous or wrong-password GET https://dash.lab.test/api/summary -> 401 with WWW-Authenticate (origin_delta=0).

cases.description: Default-deny first block for unknown Host and IP literal: requests to https://192.0.2.10:443/ with Host: unknown.lab.test and Host: 192.0.2.10 reach default-deny (404) with zero portal or dashboard content.
cases.expected_outcome: Both requests return HTTP 404 from default-deny; response body contains neither portal nor dashboard marker; dashboard origin_delta=0.

cases.description: Host case, trailing dot, explicit port, and server_names alias normalisation: Host: PORTAL.LAB.TEST, Host: portal.lab.test., Host: portal.lab.test:443, and Host: portal-alias.lab.test all select portal-home; Host: DASH.LAB.TEST. and Host: dash.lab.test:443 select dashboard and enforce Basic auth.
cases.expected_outcome: All portal Host variants return 200 with portal marker; all dashboard Host variants return 401 without credentials and 200 with valid credentials; GET /api/sharing lists both portal.lab.test and portal-alias.lab.test under one portal-home entry.

cases.description: Missing/unknown SNI and mismatched SNI vs Host: TLS handshake with unknown SNI (unknown.sni.test) or SNI=portal.lab.test while HTTP Host=dash.lab.test completes with the listener's certificate, routes by Host to dashboard, and still enforces dashboard Basic auth.
cases.expected_outcome: Unauthenticated request with SNI=portal.lab.test and Host=dash.lab.test is denied 401 (origin_delta=0); authenticated request succeeds 200.

cases.description: Path canonicalisation (dot segments, repeated slashes, percent-encoded dot segments, and percent-encoded separators %2f/%2F) and cross-vhost prefix isolation: /a/../api/summary, //api///summary, /%2e%2e/api/summary, /api%2fsummary, /api%2Fsummary, and /..%2fapi/summary on dash.lab.test require Basic auth and never bypass location auth; static root escape /..%2f..%2fetc/passwd on portal.lab.test is rejected; requesting /api/summary or /dashboard on Host: portal.lab.test returns 404 from the static root, never dashboard content.
cases.expected_outcome: POST /api/routes/test and backend observed_path agree on canonical /api/summary; unauthenticated dot-segment and %2f/%2F encoded-separator paths on dash.lab.test return 401 (origin_delta=0); portal.lab.test/api/summary and /..%2f..%2fetc/passwd return 404/400 with zero dashboard or host-file content.

cases.description: Forged X-Forwarded-For, Forwarded, RFC 9440 Client-Cert headers, and provider identity headers (Tailscale-User-Login, Cf-Access-Authenticated-User-Email, Cf-Access-Jwt-Assertion): unauthenticated requests with forged headers are denied 401; on authenticated requests, Jul overwrites X-Forwarded-For with canonical peer IP (192.0.2.11), strips Forwarded and Client-Cert/Client-Cert-Chain/X-Forwarded-Client-Cert, and forwards unknown provider headers as untrusted client input without trusting them for authorisation.
cases.expected_outcome: Forged headers without Basic auth return 401 (origin_delta=0); authenticated request shows observed_headers['x-forwarded-for']=='192.0.2.11', 'forwarded'/'client-cert' absent (stripped), and provider headers recorded as untrusted.

cases.description: Direct-origin, admin, metrics, and unconfigured-service isolation from external lab clients plus scoped firewall verification: lab-client-1 and lab-client-2 attempts to reach 192.0.2.10:3000 (backend), 192.0.2.10:9443 (admin/metrics), and 192.0.2.10:8444 (unconfigured) are rejected; scoped iptables chain JL581 counters confirm packet rejection.
cases.expected_outcome: All three ports are unreachable from lab-client-1 and lab-client-2; iptables JL581 REJECT counter increments > 0; temporarily blocking 443 in JL581 rejects traffic and restoring it recovers 200.

cases.description: Native Jul TLS chain verification negatives from external client namespace: (1) client trusting wrong-ca.pem fails TLS handshake; (2) client connecting for wrong hostname (wrong.lab.test) fails hostname verification; (3) configuring Jul with leaf-only cert (missing intermediate) causes client trusting only root-ca.pem to fail chain verification until full chain is restored.
cases.expected_outcome: All three TLS verification negative cases fail at TLS handshake before any HTTP request is sent; restoring full chain recovers verified 200.

cases.description: WAF advanced control on dashboard: (1) benign authenticated GET/POST succeeds 200 (origin_delta=+1); (2) authenticated SQLi (?q=1'+OR+'1'='1) and XSS (<script>alert(1)</script>) payloads are blocked by Coraza CRS with 403 Forbidden before reaching origin (origin_delta=0); (3) authenticated POST body > 1 MiB (request_body_limit = '1m') is rejected with 413 Request Entity Too Large before reaching origin (origin_delta=0).
cases.expected_outcome: Benign -> 200 (origin_delta=+1); SQLi/XSS -> 403 (origin_delta=0); 1.2 MiB body -> 413 (origin_delta=0).

cases.description: Rate-limit advanced control on portal: (1) paced normal load (< 50 req/s) from lab-client-1 succeeds with 100% 200 OK; (2) deliberate unpaced burst (> 180 requests) from lab-client-2 triggers 429 Too Many Requests with Retry-After while lab-client-1's independent source IP bucket and the dashboard remain unaffected.
cases.expected_outcome: Paced load returns 0x 429; deliberate burst from lab-client-2 returns 429s; concurrent probe from lab-client-1 (192.0.2.11) returns 200.

cases.description: Cache isolation and SD-16 warnings: F1 keeps Jul process-wide response cache disabled on every entry; portal emits HTTP Cache-Control: public, max-age=300 for browsers while dashboard emits Cache-Control: private, no-store and private marker JUL-F1-PRIVATE-FAMILY-TELEMETRY-DO-NOT-CACHE; cold and warm repeated requests never leak private marker to portal or excluded client; planning a candidate that enables Jul cache on restricted dashboard triggers intent_restricted_cached and cache_on_restricted_entry warnings, and overlapping cached entries trigger cache_shared_across_entries.
cases.expected_outcome: Zero private marker occurrences on portal or excluded requests across cold/warm cycles; plan/lint surfaces intent_restricted_cached, cache_on_restricted_entry, and cache_shared_across_entries warnings.

cases.description: Backend down and recovery isolation: stopping dashboard_backend.py causes authenticated dashboard requests to return 502/503 while portal continues serving 200 OK unaffected; restarting dashboard_backend.py restores 200 OK on dashboard without touching portal.
cases.expected_outcome: During backend stop: dashboard -> 502, portal -> 200; after backend start: dashboard -> 200 within 1s.

cases.description: Portal-only route/target/header change, rejection, rollback, and restart isolation: apply a portal route/location change (adding a portal sub-route and updating cache_control), reject an invalid portal edit, roll back, and restart while verifying that dashboard's audience delta is absent/unchanged (requires_acknowledgement=false) and dashboard stays restricted throughout.
cases.expected_outcome: Plan lists no widened/narrowed/uncertain delta for dashboard; dashboard remains restricted (401 excluded, 200 intended) across portal route apply, rejection, rollback, and restart.

cases.description: Deliberate dashboard-public transition, Console vs API/CLI acknowledgement contract, and exact recovery: (1) planning removal of Basic auth while keeping sharing.mode='restricted' emits intent_restricted_unenforced warning and class='widened', requires_acknowledgement=true; (2) planning CFG-F1-07 (Basic removed + sharing.mode='public') emits class='widened', declared_mode_widened=true, requires_acknowledgement=true; Console UI gates Apply behind explicit entry-named acknowledgement while API/CLI return the same server-owned fields without server-side blocking; (3) applying CFG-F1-07 makes anonymous dashboard requests return 200 (expected in public mode); (4) recovering CFG-F1-04 (class='narrowed', triggers_retirement=true) immediately restores 401 for anonymous and 200 for intended.
cases.expected_outcome: Plans report exact classes/findings/requires_acknowledgement; public mode serves anonymous 200; recovery to CFG-F1-04 retires open public streams and restores 401/200.

cases.description: Complete withdrawal via withdrawn=true and repeatable location_set_withdrawn: setting withdrawn=true on dashboard returns 403 Forbidden with Cache-Control: no-store (and no Expires), preserves proxy_pass/auth.basic/waf/sharing in config, reports GET /api/sharing withdrawn='yes', and recovers in one reversible change (location_set_withdrawn withdrawn=false).
cases.expected_outcome: Withdrawn dashboard returns 403 + Cache-Control: no-store to both anonymous and valid-credential callers (origin_delta=0); GET /api/sharing shows withdrawn='yes' and intact credential='basic', action='proxy_pass'; recovery restores 200/401.

cases.description: Outermost stage-0 withdrawal gate precedence over redirect rewrites, WASM request Stop plugin (testdata/plugins/request-block.wasm with X-Block: 1) and header-inject plugin, CORS preflight OPTIONS, and conflicting response_headers/expires: verify first when withdrawn=false that X-Block: 1 triggers request-block.wasm sdk.Stop body ('blocked by request-block plugin'), then when withdrawn=true verify the stage-0 gate answers 403 Forbidden with Cache-Control: no-store, empty body (no plugin body), no Location, no X-Plugin, and no Expires header.
cases.expected_outcome: When withdrawn=true, GET (with X-Block: 1 and /old rewrite) and OPTIONS preflight return stage-0 403 Forbidden with Cache-Control: no-store and no plugin body, Location, X-Plugin, or Expires header.

cases.description: Legacy auth.deny withdrawal mechanism, held-stream retirement, and documented limits: holding active dashboard SSE + H1 WebSocket streams and applying complete candidate CFG-F1-06 (auth.deny = ['0.0.0.0/0', '::/0'] alongside auth.basic) classifies dashboard as narrowed, retires open streams within <= 2.0s while preserving active sibling portal stream on the same H2 connection, denies fresh requests with 403 while preserving auth.basic and proxy_pass, surfaces intent_checks_bypassed when outer rewrites exist, and recovers to CFG-F1-04.
cases.expected_outcome: CFG-F1-06 retires held dashboard streams within <= 2.0s (completed_within_bound=true, collateral_count=0), returns 403 (origin_delta=0) while keeping jul_checks.credential='basic' and jul_checks.network='deny_list', surfaces intent_checks_bypassed when rewrites exist, and recovers to CFG-F1-04 (200).

cases.description: Exact-entry retirement on shared HTTP/2 connection coalescing and owned H1 WebSocket upgrades within 2s bound: establish (a) one shared TLS/HTTP/2 connection (using leaf cert covering portal.lab.test and dash.lab.test) carrying an active dashboard SSE stream AND an active portal download/stream, plus (b) an owned HTTP/1.1 101 WebSocket session to dash.lab.test/ws; publish withdrawal (CFG-F1-05); verify dashboard H2 stream and H1 WebSocket close within <= 2.0s from Publish (with RFC 6455 1008 Close handshake counted in graceful_count), while the sibling portal stream on the same H2 connection continues to completion with collateral_count=0 and claim='complete_withdrawal'.
cases.expected_outcome: ended_exchanges >= 2, completed_within_bound=true, collateral_count=0, keep_open=false, claim='complete_withdrawal'; client event log confirms dashboard closure <= 2000ms from Publish and uninterrupted completion of the shared-connection portal exchange.

cases.description: mTLS shared-listener variant (CFG-F1-08, client_auth.mode='request' + require_client_cert=true on dashboard): (1) GET /api/sharing reports client_auth_request_mode_shared warning on portal-home; (2) portal-home succeeds 200 without client cert; (3) dashboard without client cert is denied 403 on that stream; (4) dashboard with client-wrong-ca.crt fails TLS handshake; (5) dashboard with client-unauthorised-san.crt fails handshake; (6) dashboard with client-intended.crt and client-revoked.crt (before revocation) succeeds 200.
cases.expected_outcome: Shared listener enforces require_client_cert per location, surfaces client_auth_request_mode_shared warning, rejects untrusted/wrong-SAN certs at handshake, denies cert-less dashboard requests with 403, and admits valid certs with 200.

cases.description: mTLS CRL revocation reload — handshake refusal AND per-request policy re-check on both open HTTP/2 and open HTTP/1.1 keep-alive connections (#642/#563): keep both an open shared HTTP/2 connection (with active backpressured 256 KiB portal stream + dashboard SSE stream) AND an open HTTP/1.1 keep-alive connection + H1 SSE stream authenticated with client-revoked.crt; replace tls/clients.crl with tls/clients-revoked.crl and reload Jul; verify: (a) active H2 and H1 SSE streams on dashboard are retired within <= 2.0s from Publish (completed_within_bound=true, collateral_count=0); (b) the next request to dash.lab.test on BOTH the already-open H2 connection and the already-open H1 keep-alive connection is denied with 403 Forbidden per-request without a new handshake, while the active 256 KiB portal stream and post-reload portal requests on the same H2 connection succeed 200; (c) a new TLS handshake with client-revoked.crt is rejected at handshake; (d) client-intended.crt continues to succeed 200.
cases.expected_outcome: Publish-time CRL revocation retires active H2 and H1 dashboard streams within <= 2.0s (completed_within_bound=true), denies next request on existing H2 and H1 keep-alive connections with 403 while active sibling H2 portal stream completes 262,144 bytes, rejects new handshake for revoked cert, and admits intended cert.

cases.description: mTLS dedicated-listener variant (CFG-F1-09) admission, default-deny, held-stream retirement, and recovery: portal on 192.0.2.10:443 has client_auth.mode='none' (no CertificateRequest sent to browsers, no client_auth_request_mode_shared warning); dashboard on 192.0.2.10:8443 has default-deny-mtls first block + client_auth.mode='require' + require_client_cert=true; uncertified clients fail handshake on :8443 while certified intended client gets 200 on dash.lab.test:8443 and 404 on unknown Host on :8443; holding an active SSE + H1 WebSocket session on :8443 and withdrawing dashboard retires open streams within <= 2.0s (completed_within_bound=true) and recovers cleanly.
cases.expected_outcome: Portal on :443 has zero client-cert prompt and no client_auth_request_mode_shared warning; :8443 enforces mandatory mTLS handshake, default-deny-mtls, and <= 2.0s held-stream retirement on withdrawal + recovery.

cases.description: htpasswd file-content lifecycle and publish-time retirement: (1) both family-intended and family-guest authenticate 200; (2) overwrite dashboard.htpasswd on disk with dashboard-revoked.htpasswd (removing family-guest) WITHOUT reloading Jul -> family-guest still gets 200 and postcondition evaluate still reports candidate_serving (postconditions do not reread files, RR12); (3) hold an active SSE stream as family-guest and trigger explicit reload -> publish-time content classification detects user removal ('narrowed'), retires the open dashboard SSE stream within <= 2s, denies family-guest with 401 (origin_delta=0), and keeps family-intended working with 200.
cases.expected_outcome: Before reload: family-guest -> 200; on reload: active stream retired <= 2s (ended_exchanges >= 1, completed_within_bound=true), family-guest -> 401, family-intended -> 200.

cases.description: Constituent-reason keep_open_entries eligibility and mandatory-tightening override: (1) pure uncertain change (e.g. upstream/target change alone) sets keep_open_eligible=true and honours keep_open_entries=['dashboard'] (skipping retirement, setting keep_open=true, and forfeiting complete_withdrawal claim); (2) mixed change combining an uncertain change with a mandatory tightening (e.g. adding CIDR restriction or withdrawn=true or publish-time htpasswd removal) sets keep_open_eligible=false, overrides any supplied keep_open_entries=['dashboard'], and retires open exchanges within <= 2s.
cases.expected_outcome: Pure uncertain change honours keep_open_entries with keep_open=true; mixed mandatory-tightening + uncertain change overrides keep_open_entries and retires open exchanges within 2s.

cases.description: Protocol matrix verification on F1: real-client verification of HTTP/1.1, TLS ALPN HTTP/2, SSE over HTTP/1.1 AND SSE over HTTP/2, and H1 WebSocket (RFC 6455 Upgrade, including idle stability past 0.55s and Close 1008 retirement) through Jul to the dashboard origin; explicit record of non-F1 protocols (native gRPC, HTTP/3, L4 stream) with owner test evidence.
cases.expected_outcome: HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2 (ALPN h2), SSE over HTTP/1.1, SSE over HTTP/2, and H1 WebSocket all succeed for intended client and are denied for excluded client; Jul -> plaintext origin uses HTTP/1.1.

cases.description: W0 Idle profile: 5-minute settle followed by 10-minute idle measurement (5s scrape interval via soak-scrape.go + cgroup/proc snapshots); establish last-5-minute median reference for CPU, RSS, Go heap, goroutines, open FDs, and jul_listener_conns.
cases.expected_outcome: Zero scrape errors, zero gaps > 2 intervals, zero restarts; baseline W0 reference medians recorded.

cases.description: W1 Representative load profile: 16 closed-loop workers, 2-minute warm-up followed by 10-minute measurement; 70% portal HTML (~4 KiB), 10% portal asset (256 KiB), 20% authorised dashboard JSON (~2 KiB), paced across client addresses below F1's 50 req/s per-IP rate limit.
cases.expected_outcome: Zero request errors, zero 429s, 100% 200 OK across all three classes; latency p50/p95/p99, throughput, CPU, RSS, heap, goroutines, FDs, and cgroup stats within predeclared bounds.

cases.description: W2 Mixed + long-lived connections profile: W1 representative mix plus 10% excluded-identity dashboard requests (verified 401 denied before origin) and 20 held long-lived dashboard connections (10 SSE + 10 H1 WebSocket).
cases.expected_outcome: 100% of excluded requests denied with 401 (zero succeeding); 100% of intended portal/dashboard requests succeed 200; all 20 held long-lived connections stay established until W3 withdrawal.

cases.description: W3 Access-change and complete-withdrawal continuity profile: during W2 (with 20 held dashboard connections and an active shared-H2 portal+dashboard connection), withdraw dashboard access (withdrawn=true), hold for 2 minutes, then restore (withdrawn=false), while probing portal.lab.test once per second from an independent rate-limit bucket (192.0.2.13).
cases.expected_outcome: Zero failed portal 1 req/s continuity probes; 100% of fresh dashboard requests sent after terminal applied_live denied with 403 + Cache-Control: no-store; all 20 held dashboard connections + shared-H2 dashboard stream retired within <= 2.0s from Publish with collateral_count=0 and claim='complete_withdrawal'; restoration recovers 200 for intended and 401 for excluded with zero Jul restarts.

cases.description: W4 Outage, recovery, and post-drain quiescence profile: during representative traffic with 1 req/s portal and dashboard probes, stop dashboard backend for 60 seconds (portal stays 100% 200 OK; dashboard returns 502), restart backend (first successful dashboard probe within <= 10s of backend readiness), then stop all load/held clients, wait >= 95s (> 90s upstream idle timeout), and measure 2-minute post-drain median against W0 reference.
cases.expected_outcome: Zero failed portal probes during 60s backend outage; dashboard recovers 200 OK within <= 10s of backend readiness; after drain, jul_http_requests_in_flight=0 and jul_upstream_connections=0; goroutine growth <= 4*16+32 (96), heap growth <= 64 MiB, FD delta within predeclared +8 tolerance.

cases.description: Spec §14 T1–T6 automated surface rehearsal and author dry-run record: (a) automated task verification confirming GET /api/sharing, plan/apply, and postcondition evaluate expose all required facts for T1–T6 (labeled as automated rehearsal with human effort marked unmeasured); (b) separate observed author dry run (t1-t6-author-rehearsal.json) recording actual author task execution times, decisions, handoffs, and recurring maintenance duties without claiming #585 independent fresh-operator study completion.
cases.expected_outcome: Automated surface verification and separate author dry-run record both pass with explicit provenance separation between script automation, author rehearsal, and #585 independent operator study.

cases.description: Downstream handoff artifacts (#634, #582, #583, #613) and validated documentation/issue disposition inventories: verify docs/sharing/f1-handoff-interfaces.json, docs/sharing/f1-standalone-runbook.md, docs/sharing/f1-standalone-evidence.md, docs-check.py, and explicit affected-document and affected-issue disposition inventories.

cases.description: File-owned SIGHUP held-stream retirement and file-owned restart postcondition lifecycle: under jul-readonly.service (CFG-F1-10), hold active shared-H2 portal (backpressured 256 KiB) + dashboard SSE stream + H1 WebSocket session; install CFG-F1-11 (withdrawn=true) on disk and send SIGHUP -> verify dashboard SSE and H1 WebSocket retire within <= 2.0s (completed_within_bound=true, collateral_count=0, claim='complete_withdrawal') while the active portal stream on the same H2 connection completes all 262,144 bytes; then restart jul-readonly.service -> verify boot_id changes, pre-restart postcondition evaluates to unverifiable, and re-plan evaluates to candidate_serving.
cases.expected_outcome: File-owned SIGHUP withdrawal retires held SSE + H1 WebSocket within <= 2.0s while active sibling H2 portal stream completes 262,144 bytes; file-owned restart rotates boot_id, marks pre-restart postcondition unverifiable, and confirms candidate_serving on re-plan.

cases.description: File-owned mTLS shared-listener (CFG-F1-12) and dedicated-listener (CFG-F1-13) verification: under jul-readonly.service, verify (1) CFG-F1-12 shared-listener mTLS admission (anonymous portal 200, cert-less dashboard 403, intended/pre-revoked cert 200), mutating API refusal (409 config_authority_read_only), and SIGHUP CRL revocation reload retiring active held stream within <= 2.0s and denying open connection with 403; (2) CFG-F1-13 dedicated-listener mTLS (:8443) startup under jul-readonly.service, portal :443 client_auth='none', dashboard :8443 mandatory mTLS admission and default-deny-mtls, and cgroup/RSS/FD snapshot.
cases.expected_outcome: Both file-owned mTLS configurations (CFG-F1-12 and CFG-F1-13) enforce read-only authority (409 on API mutations), verify mTLS admission/denial, and retire active streams within <= 2.0s on SIGHUP CRL reload.
